findings.summary: A baseline entry the core could not run, or that timed out, would count as a real failure on the base.
findings.evidence: In checks.rs:243-251, baseline_runs records a check that could not start as passed=false with the note 'baseline check could not run: {e}'. The Baseline doc comment (records.rs:1901) says timeouts are also recorded as not passed, with a note. The plan's failed_before returns false only when the baseline-level note is set. It does not look at the entry's own note, so a check that could not start on the base would make a real failure at verification pre-existing. Fix: Make failed_before also return false when the matching entry could not run: either its note starts with 'baseline check could not run', or it has exit_code None. Add that case to the criterion 6 unit tests.

findings.summary: Two places decide whether a check is pre-existing: judge recomputes it from the baseline, and run.rs separately writes the note mark. They can drift apart.
findings.evidence: The plan has judge take the baseline and decide pre-existing itself, and has mark_pre_existing put the note on check_runs first. The base_commit filter lives only in run.rs, so a judge caller could get a different answer from what run.rs would mark. Fix: Have judge and mark_pre_existing both call one is_pre_existing(check, baseline) function. Put the base_commit check inside it too, for example by comparing against a base commit passed in VerdictInputs, so a mismatched baseline is ignored everywhere.

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG demonstration only reads the entry; it shows the entry exists.
findings.evidence: 'Run: git diff CHANGELOG.md. Observes: A plain-language entry says ...' This is a content criterion, so reading it is acceptable, but the check fails only if the entry is missing. Fix: Name what the reader must find: that base-failing checks are marked pre-existing and no longer reject a job, and that the verifier judges every criterion even when a check fails. Also require the entry to be under the Unreleased heading.

summary: I read verify.rs (VerdictInputs, judge), run.rs (the closing.baseline field, take_baseline, how verification runs its checks, and the `if all_passed` gate on the verifier), records.rs (Baseline) and checks.rs (baseline_runs). The plan changes the two places where the fault starts. In judge, line 255 currently adds a "check X failed" reason for every failed check. In run.rs, line 1780 runs the verifier only when every check passed. Without the verifier there is no output, so judge writes "the verifier did not assess this criterion" for every criterion (line 286). The plan's demonstrations would fail without the change, and no athena.toml or schema change is needed, because the mark goes in CheckRun.note and CheckRun is deny_unknown_fields. The work fits one producer run. Remaining issues are minor: a baseline entry whose own note says the check could not run is still counted as pre-existing; the plan has the pre-existing decision in two places; and the CHANGELOG demonstration only reads the entry.
